 Follow Glenn Close’s Daughter Annie Starke Wows in a Stunning Red Carpet Look as Her Mom Gets Major Honor
 Megan Johnson Mon, November 16, 2026 at 3:37 AM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Glenn Close just hit the red carpet alongside her stunning daughter, Annie Starke , as she received a major honor.
 Close, 79, is known for roles in films like  Dangerous Liaisons ,  Fatal Attraction , The Big Chill , and  Hillbilly Elegy . As the star, who has been nominated for eight Academy Awards, hit the red carpet at the 17th Governors Awards on Sunday, it was her daughter, Starke, who joined her in the spotlight. Boasting bronzed skin, golden hair, and a stunning silver gown, Starke, 38, was reminiscent of her mother during some of her most famous roles back in the '80s.
 Check out the glowing mother/daughter duo below:
 CHRIS DELMAS / Getty Images

 Close Received a Major Honor at the Ceremony
 The Governors Awards, which celebrate some of the biggest names in Hollywood, are a major event held by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences. As the AP noted , the Governors Awards often go to artists with extraordinary careers but no competitive Oscar, such as Tom Cruise , who was honored last year. Close received the special honor of Sunday and gave a speech before the crowd. Upon announcing Close as this year's special honoree, the Academy noted her vast list of film credentials.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "Throughout her extraordinary body of work, Glenn Close's unparalleled emotional range has brought to life some of the most complex characters in cinema," they shared in a statement .
 Michael Buckner / Getty Images
 Michael Douglas Felt Close Deserved an Oscar for Fatal Attraction 
 Close broke boundaries in 1987's Fatal Attraction alongside Michael Douglas . In the film, Douglas plays Dan, a family man who enters an affair with Alex Forrest . While Dan thinks he has the perfect weekend affair, it turns into a nightmare when Alex proves to be emotionally disturbed. During a recent appearance on the Graham Norton Show that reunited the duo, Douglas made it clear that he felt Close deserved to win the Oscar that year over Cher , who won for Moonstruck .
 "She should have won with Fatal Attraction ," Douglas said.
 When Douglas noted that Cher won instead, Norton said, "Oh wow."
 Advertisement Advertisement "I know. That's what we all said," Douglas replied.
